anomalies.observed: Q1 (P-MOSFET) has its source (Q1.2, pin S) on +5V and its drain (Q1.3, pin D) on USBC_VBUS_IN. The LTC4412 VIN pin (U6.1) is on USBC_VBUS_IN and SENSE (U6.6) is on +5V. The other PMOS load switches in the design (Q6 and Q9) place the input rail on the source and the switched output on the drain.
anomalies.expected: For an ideal-diode OR-ing stage with an LTC4412 and a P-channel MOSFET, the input (USB VBUS) should sit on the MOSFET source and the load/output on the drain. The body diode then blocks reverse current from +5V back to VBUS, which is the reverse-current protection the spec says this stage exists to provide.

evidence.quote: USBC_VBUS_IN [High Power] : J3.A4(VBUS,passive) ... Q1.3(D,passive) R11.1(passive) R64.2(2,passive) U25.5(VBUS,passive) U6.1(VIN,power_in)

anomalies.impact: With the MOSFET source on the +5V side, its body diode conducts from +5V back toward VBUS whenever the FET is off. This allows backfeed from the 5V rail into the USB input and defeats the intended reverse-current protection, so the USB power path would not behave as designed.

anomalies.observed: The second LED of dual LED D30 (A2, pin 4) sits directly on ESTOP_OUT. Its cathode K2 (pin 2) returns through R60 to the same ESTOP_OUT net, so both terminals of that LED are at the same node and it can never conduct.
anomalies.expected: A status LED in the e-stop output path should have its anode and cathode on different nets, with the series resistor between the driven node and the far end of the LED.

evidence.quote: ESTOP_OUT : D30.4(A2,input) J13.6(Pin_6,passive) J2.6(Pin_6,passive) R60.2(passive) U36.4(Y,output)

anomalies.impact: The e-stop indicator LED on this channel is dead, so the operator gets no visual confirmation from that channel. The loop also places a 130R resistor across the same node with no useful current path.
